messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — the biweekly release train scheduled for Mon 2026-08-03 overlaps with the EU company holiday. Can we shift the cutoff one day earlier or move the train to Tue?
kevin: +1 to shifting cutoff earlier. Branch freeze on Fri is tight for some teams. Who's impacted?
anya: FYI backend team has a migration planned that needs a Monday deploy, so moving to Tue would be better for us.
tim: If we move to Tue we need to update cadence calendar and the on-call bridge. I can cover the bridge change but need 24h notice.
sasha: Can we do a smaller change: move cutoff to Thu EOD instead of Fri? That avoids moving the whole train. Thoughts?
maria: Proposal: either A) Cutoff Thu 23:59 UTC, release train Mon as planned but only critical patches on Mon; or B) Move train to Tue (2-day shift) with cutoff Fri EOD. Which is lower risk?
kevin: For customer-facing feature freezes, A is safer. For migrations (anya) B is better. Maybe opt for A and let teams request exceptions with a flagged PR label `release/exception`.
anya: That works — we'll mark the migration PR with `release/exception` and ping release lead.
calendar-bot: Reminder: updating release calendar requires a calendar-admin +1 and will send notices to #general. Run `./scripts/update-calendar --release 2026.08b --cutoff 2026-07-30`
tim: I'll handle the calendar update and bridge change if we go with A. Will post updated calendar + notice by EOD PDT. :thumbsup:
maria: Awesome. Action items: 1) Tim update calendar + bridge. 2) Kevin add PR label guidance to release notes. 3) Any team needing exception file PR with `release/exception` and ping. I'll send a short note in #eng and tag owners.
kevin: Also nudge on changelog — I'll do a quick reminder in the changelog doc to double-check version bumps before cutoff.
maria: Thanks all. Closing — we'll treat A as default unless someone posts an objection here by 12:00 UTC tomorrow.
